info.title: Valyu API
info.description:
The search API built for AI agents. One API that gives your AI unified access to web search, academic papers, financial data, SEC filings, clinical trials, patents, genomics, and 40+ proprietary data sources.

## Products

| Product | Endpoint | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Search** | `POST /v1/search` | Multi-source search across web and proprietary datasets |
| **Contents** | `POST /v1/contents` | Extract clean, structured content from URLs |
| **Answer** | `POST /v1/answer` | AI-powered answers with real-time search |
| **DeepResearch** | `POST /v1/deepresearch/tasks` | Async research agents for comprehensive analysis |
| **Workflows** (Beta) | `GET /v1/workflows` | Templated, versioned DeepResearch for repeatable knowledge work |
| **Datasources** | `GET /v1/datasources` | Discover available data sources and their schemas |

## Authentication

All endpoints require an API key passed via the `X-API-Key` header (the lowercase `x-api-key` form is also accepted). Get your key at [platform.valyu.ai](https://platform.valyu.ai).

```
X-API-Key: your_api_key_here
```

## Pricing

Pay per use in credits. One credit balance covers every API.
- **Search**: priced per result returned. Web and news results use 0.1 credits each (100 per 1,000 results). arXiv, PubMed, bioRxiv and medRxiv use 0.05 credits each (50 per 1,000). Other datasets have their own price per 1,000 results, listed in `GET /v1/datasources` (`pricing.cpm`).
- **Contents**: 0.2 credits per successfully extracted URL, plus 0.2 credits per URL when `summary` (AI summary or structured extraction) is enabled. Failed URLs are free.
- **Answer**: no per-request fee. You pay for the search, content extraction and AI processing each answer uses, reported in `cost.total_deduction_dollars`.
- **DeepResearch**: fixed price per task by mode: instant 8 credits, fast 25, standard 100, heavy 500, max 2,500, plus tool add-ons.

Every plan includes web search and open academic sources. Paid plans unlock specialist sources such as SEC filings, clinical trials, patents and genomics. See [pricing](https://docs.valyu.ai/pricing) for plans and free credits.

## Rate limits

Limits apply per organisation: 10 requests per second with bursts up to 20, and 86,400 requests per day by default. Enterprise plans can raise them. A request over the limit is currently rejected with `403 Forbidden` and the body `{"error": "Forbidden", "message": "Access denied - API key is invalid, disabled, or revoked"}`. If a key that otherwise works starts receiving 403 under load, reduce concurrency and retry with exponential backoff.

## SDKs

- [Python SDK](https://pypi.org/project/valyu/) - `pip install valyu`
- [TypeScript SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/valyu-js) - `npm install valyu-js`

tags.description: **Beta.** Templated, versioned DeepResearch for repeatable knowledge work - earnings previews, diligence reads, market sizings. A workflow bundles a prompt template with typed variables, a research strategy, report format, deliverables, tools, and a recommended mode. Workflows are immutably versioned; runs can pin a version. Two scopes exist: your organization's private workflows and curated Valyu workflows available to everyone. Run a workflow by passing `workflow_id` + `workflow_params` to `POST /v1/deepresearch/tasks` - same auth, billing, and task lifecycle as freeform DeepResearch.

403.description:
The key is disabled, revoked or lacks permission, or the requested sources are not available to this key.

- `tier_insufficient` - every requested dataset is above your plan. If only some are, those are skipped, the rest are searched and the response carries a `datasets_not_in_plan` warning. `recovery` has `current_plan`, `required_plan` (`{id, name, price}` or `null`), `required_tier` and `upgrade_url`.
- `dataset_unavailable` - every requested dataset is licensed or unknown. `recovery` has `current_plan`, `contact_url` and `datasources_url`.
- `dataset_outside_task_scope` - with `scope_policy: "strict"`, at least one listed dataset is outside your plan or grants. Strict scope never falls back to a partial search.
- `deepresearch_only` - every requested dataset is DeepResearch-only. Mixed with other sources, DeepResearch-only datasets are skipped with a `datasets_deepresearch_only` warning.

A request over the rate limit returns `429`, not `403`.

post.description:
Extract content from URLs, with optional summaries, structured extraction and screenshots. Access or extraction can fail for individual URLs.

- **Synchronous:** Submit up to 10 URLs and receive results directly.
- **Asynchronous:** Set `async: true` for up to 50 URLs, save the returned `job_id` and poll the job endpoint. Requests with more than 10 URLs must use `async: true`.
- **Partial success:** Inspect the result for each URL rather than treating the request as all-or-nothing.

**Pricing:** 0.2 credits per successfully extracted URL, plus 0.2 credits per URL when `summary` is enabled. Failed URLs are free. `total_cost_dollars` is the amount charged.

post.summary: Get AI-powered answers with real-time search
post.description:
Searches across web, academic, and financial sources, then uses AI to generate a readable, cited response. Returns results as a **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** stream.

The AI agent performs multi-round search with up to 2 tool call rounds (3 in `fast_mode`), can decompose queries into sub-queries, and synthesizes findings into a coherent answer.

## SSE Event Types

Events are sent as `data: {json}\n\n` with the following types:

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `search_results` | Search sources found (may occur multiple times) |
| `content` | Partial answer text chunk (OpenAI-compatible delta format) |
| `metadata` | Final metadata with costs, token usage, all search results and any `warnings` |
| `error` | `{"error": "Streaming failed"}` if the answer fails mid-stream; the stream then ends |
| `[DONE]` | Stream complete |

## Cost Structure

There is no per-request fee. Each answer is charged for the search, content extraction and AI processing it uses. `cost.total_deduction_dollars` in the final `metadata` event is the amount billed, and each search result is billed once per answer. `data_max_price` caps only the search component, not the entire charge.

value.query: What are the latest FDA-approved treatments for type 2 diabetes?
Compare the top 5 electric vehicles by range and price in 2024
SEC enforcement actions against crypto exchanges
value.system_instructions: You are a financial regulatory analyst. Focus on enforcement actions and penalties.

200.description: SSE stream of search results, answer chunks, and metadata.

schema.description:
Server-Sent Events stream. Each event has format: `data: {json}\n\n`

**search_results event:**
```json
{"search_results": [{"title": "...", "url": "...", "content": "...", ...}]}
```

**content event (OpenAI-compatible):**
```json
{"choices": [{"delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "text chunk"}, "index": 0}]}
```

**metadata event:**
```json
{"success": true, "tx_id": "ai_tx_...", "original_query": "...", "contents": "Full answer text...", "search_results": [{"title": "...", "url": "...", "content": "...", "description": "...", "source": "web", "source_type": "website", "data_type": "unstructured", "date": "...", "length": 1200, "image_url": {}}], "search_metadata": {"tx_ids": ["tx_..."], "number_of_results": 10, "total_characters": 50000}, "ai_usage": {"input_tokens": 15000, "output_tokens": 2000}, "cost": {"total_deduction_dollars": 0.0475, "search_deduction_dollars": 0.00625, "ai_deduction_dollars": 0.03625, "contents_deduction_dollars": 0.005}}
```

`contents` is the full answer (JSON text when `structured_output` is set). `total_deduction_dollars` is the amount billed. When the searches behind the answer skipped or adjusted something, the metadata event also carries `warnings`: the warnings of those searches, deduplicated, in the same `{type, message, detail}` shape as Search. See [Warnings](https://docs.valyu.ai/api-reference/warnings).

**error event:**
```json
{"error": "Streaming failed"}
```

**done signal:**
```
data: [DONE]
```

post.description:
Start an asynchronous investigation that retrieves information and produces a cited report, with optional generated files. Provide the research question, source controls and output requirements.

Save the returned task ID and poll the status endpoint or configure a completion webhook. Execution time depends on the mode and task; handle queued, running and terminal states rather than relying on a fixed duration.

**Billing.** When the task is created, its mode's base price is held against your balance. The hold is released when the task is charged, or when it ends without a charge. If your balance, minus amounts held for your other queued and running tasks, is below the price, or the charge would exceed your monthly usage limit, the request returns 402 and no task is created. If billing can't be checked, it returns 503 with no task created; retry with backoff.

Completed tasks are charged the mode price plus tool add-ons. Failed tasks are free. Cancelling a `running` or `awaiting_input` task charges the full mode price; cancelling a `queued` or `paused` task is free.

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key for authentication. Get yours at [platform.valyu.ai](https://platform.valyu.ai).

Error.description: Error response. Every error body has `error`. Search, Contents, Answer and Datasources errors usually also carry `success: false`. Errors returned before a request reaches the endpoint (missing, invalid or disabled keys, rate limits) and DeepResearch errors have no `success` field. Some errors add a machine-readable `code` and a `recovery` object.

error.description: Error message, or a machine-readable code for some errors (for example `invalid_scope_policy`, or `rate_limited` on a `429`).

message.description: Human-readable detail. Present on errors returned before the request reaches the endpoint.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, when available. Branch on this rather than on the message text.

recovery.description: Links or details that help resolve the error, when available.

transaction_id.description: Transaction ID for support, when available.

Warning.description: Something the request skipped or adjusted. A warning means the request succeeded. New `type` values may be added at any time, so handle unknown ones by showing `message`. See [Warnings](https://docs.valyu.ai/api-reference/warnings).

type.description: Stable snake_case warning type, for example `datasets_not_in_plan`. New types may be added at any time.

message.description: Self-contained sentence, safe to show a user or for an agent to relay as-is.
message.example: Your Pay-as-you-go plan doesn't include valyu/valyu-chemrxiv (Comfortably Pro, $99/mo), so it was skipped. Results come from your other sources. Comfortably Pro ($99/mo) includes it: https://platform.valyu.ai/user/account/billing?tab=plan

detail.description: Optional type-specific structured fields, including any URLs.

query.description: The search query to execute. Supports natural language queries.

max_num_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Higher limits (up to 100) are available on request. A value above your limit is lowered to it, and the response carries a `max_num_results_capped` warning.

search_type.description:
Controls which data sources are searched.

- `all` - Web and proprietary sources (default). An LLM router selects the best sources for your query.
- `web` - Web search only. Best for current events and general topics.
- `proprietary` - Academic, financial, and premium sources only. Best for research and technical analysis.
- `news` - News articles only. Best for recent news and current events.

max_price.description:
Caps the cost of the whole request. This is not a token limit or a per-result ceiling. When omitted, the default is 1000. See [pricing](https://docs.valyu.ai/pricing).

Before searching, the request is checked against its worst-case cost and rejected with 400 (`Insufficient max_price. Search requires max_price >= X for your query`) if the budget is too low. For example, 10 web results need `max_price >= 6.25`.

relevance_threshold.description: Minimum relevance score (0.0-1.0) for results after reranking. Results below this threshold are filtered out.

included_sources.description:
Sources to include in the search. Accepts:
- Domain names or URLs for web filtering (e.g. `"arxiv.org"`, `"https://arxiv.org"`)
- Dataset identifiers for proprietary sources (e.g. `"valyu/valyu-arxiv"`)
- Preset names that expand to curated source groups: `"academic"`, `"finance"`, `"patent"`, `"transportation"`, `"politics"`, `"legal"`, `"health"`, `"genomics"`, `"chemistry"`, `"physics"`
- `"web"` keyword to explicitly include web search alongside proprietary sources
- `"collection:NAME"` to reference an org-scoped saved source collection

With the default `scope_policy: "advisory"`, a list of two or more dataset IDs is treated as guidance: Valyu may search only the most relevant of them for the query. Set `scope_policy: "strict"` to search every listed dataset.

Datasets above your plan are dropped; if none remain, the request returns 403 `tier_insufficient`. DeepResearch-only datasets are dropped when listed alongside other sources, and return 403 when they are the only sources requested.

Note: most specialised and proprietary sources require a subscription. All plans include web search and open academic sources (arXiv, PubMed).

excluded_sources.description: Sources to exclude from the search. Accepts domain names, URLs, dataset identifiers and preset names (e.g. `"finance"`, `"academic"`). Excluded datasets and presets are never searched. With `scope_policy: "strict"`, only dataset identifiers are accepted, and they are removed from the `included_sources` list.

scope_policy.description:
How `included_sources` is applied to datasets.

- `advisory` (default) - `included_sources` guides source selection. With two or more dataset IDs, Valyu may search only the most relevant of them.
- `strict` - search exactly the dataset IDs in `included_sources`, minus any in `excluded_sources`. Requires 1-128 dataset IDs. Presets, domains, URLs, `"web"` and `search_type: "web"` are rejected, and web search is skipped. The response includes a `source_scope` receipt.

Strict errors: 400 `invalid_scope_policy` (unknown value), 400 `invalid_strict_source_scope` (missing, empty or oversized list, a non-dataset entry, or nothing left after exclusions), 400 `unsupported_strict_source` (a dataset Search cannot serve), and 403 `dataset_outside_task_scope` (a dataset outside your plan or grants; no partial fallback).

Not yet in the Python or TypeScript SDKs. Send it in the request body over HTTP.

source_biases.description: Bias values for specific sources to influence ranking without hard filtering. Keys are domains (e.g., 'nasa.gov') or URL paths (e.g., 'nih.gov/research'). Values are integers from -5 (strong demotion) to +5 (strong boost). Most specific path match wins.

instructions.description: Natural language instructions to help rank results by relevance to user intent. Acts as a system prompt for the search. Max 500 characters. Ignored when fast_mode is true.
instructions.example: Focus on oncology clinical trials from 2023 onwards

category.description: **Deprecated.** Use `instructions` instead. Falls back to this value if `instructions` is not set.

is_tool_call.description: Indicates whether this request originates from an AI tool call. Affects query rewriting behavior.

response_length.description:
Controls the maximum character length of content per result.

- `"short"` - 25,000 characters (default)
- `"medium"` - 50,000 characters
- `"large"` - 100,000 characters
- `"max"` - No limit
- Any positive integer for a custom character limit

start_date.description: Filter results published on or after this date. Accepts `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO-8601 datetime. Sub-day timestamps require `historical_cache: true`. If set without `end_date`, `end_date` defaults to today.

end_date.description: Filter results published on or before this date. Accepts `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO-8601 datetime. Sub-day timestamps require `historical_cache: true`. If set without `start_date`, `start_date` defaults to `1900-01-01`. `start_date` must be on or before `end_date`.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for geo-targeted web search results.

fast_mode.description: Skip query rewriting and reranking for lower latency. Searches the web and financial data in parallel. Cannot be used with `search_type: "proprietary"`.

url_only.description: Return only URLs without full content extraction. Only available when `search_type` is `"web"` or `"news"`. Skips reranking.

historical_cache.description: Prefer cached content captured within the requested date window instead of the latest crawl. Requires a date range. With the default historical_cache_strict="prefer", a result can fall back to a live crawl when no suitable snapshot exists. Use "only" to drop results without a qualifying snapshot; neither mode guarantees complete historical coverage or reproduces an entire past search index.

historical_cache_strict.description: Snapshot policy when historical_cache is true. "prefer" uses an in-window snapshot when available and otherwise may fall back to a live crawl. "only" drops results without a snapshot captured at or before the end-date cutoff. "off" disables strict snapshot filtering. Empty results are possible in every mode. For backtests, inspect record dates and snapshot evidence; publication-date filters alone do not establish point-in-time validity.

include_abstracts.description: Expand PubMed search from papers with available full text to the complete abstract corpus. Results include the abstract and, when full text is available, the most relevant full-text chunks. Has no effect on other sources.

include_image_links.description: Keep image URLs in the content. When `true` (default), images stay as markdown, for example `![Product photo](https://example.com/p.jpg)`. When `false`, each image becomes `[Image: Product photo]`. The API removes the image URL and keeps the alt text. The API removes an image with no alt text. A linked image `[![alt](src)](href)` becomes `[[Image: alt]](href)`. Other links do not change. Set `false` to use fewer tokens.

hls_coverage.description: Coverage for Wiley Health & Life Sciences (`wiley/wiley-hls`) searches. `hls` returns licensed Wiley content only. `increased_coverage` blends it with open-access biomedical literature in one ranked result set. See [Wiley HLS](https://docs.valyu.ai/guides/wiley-hls).

SearchResult.description: A single search result with extracted content.

id.description: Unique identifier for this result (typically the URL).

content.description: Extracted text content in markdown format, truncated to `response_length`.
content.example: Placeholder content representing the text returned from a source.

description.description: Short description or meta summary of the document.
description.example: Illustrative metadata, not a factual research finding.

source.description: Source identifier. `"web"` for web results, or a proprietary source name.

price.description: Cost charged for this individual result.

image_url.description: Image URLs associated with this result, keyed by index. `null` if no images.

relevance_score.description: Relevance score from reranking (0.0-1.0). Higher is more relevant.

source_type.description:
Classification of the source.

- `website` - General web page
- `forum` - Forum or discussion thread
- `paper` - Academic paper
- `data` - Structured data source
- `report` - Report or analysis
- `health_data` - Healthcare data
- `clinical_trial` - Clinical trial record
- `drug_label` - FDA drug label
- `grants` - Research grant

publication_date.description: Publication date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, or empty string if unknown.

crawl_date.description: When the page was crawled (web results). With `historical_cache`, it is second-precision and never later than the `end_date` cutoff.

abstract.description: Document-level abstract for academic results when available.
abstract.example: Placeholder abstract; the actual abstract depends on the returned paper.

metadata.description: Additional structured metadata (financial and specialized results only).

SearchResponse.description: Search response containing results and metadata.

error.description: Error or warning message. May be non-empty even on successful responses if some sources had issues.

tx_id.description: Transaction ID for tracking and support.

results_by_source.description: Count of results broken down by source type.

total_deduction_dollars.description: Total cost charged for this search.

total_characters.description: Sum of all result content lengths in characters.

warnings.description: What the search skipped or adjusted, for example named datasets outside your plan. Present only when there is something to say. New warning types may be added at any time. See [Warnings](https://docs.valyu.ai/api-reference/warnings).

source_scope.description: Receipt for a `scope_policy: "strict"` request. Present only for strict requests. It shows which datasets were dispatched and which returned rows. It does not certify full coverage: a dataset with no returned rows was not necessarily searched and found empty.

selected_dataset_ids.description: In-scope datasets the search was dispatched to.

completed_dataset_ids.description: Datasets confirmed as fully searched. Currently always empty.

returned_dataset_ids.description: Datasets that contributed at least one returned result.

omitted_dataset_ids.description: In-scope datasets that were not dispatched.

exhaustive.description: Whether the search is certified exhaustive. Currently always `false`.

errors.description: One entry per dataset that failed during the search (max 32).

urls.description: URLs to extract content from. Must be valid HTTP/HTTPS URLs. Duplicates are silently removed.

response_length.description:
Maximum character length of extracted content per URL.

- `"short"` - 25,000 characters (default)
- `"medium"` - 50,000 characters
- `"large"` - 100,000 characters
- `"max"` - No limit
- Any positive integer for a custom character limit

max_price_dollars.description:
Maximum budget for this request. Defaults to 2x the maximum possible cost.

- If the worst-case cost exceeds this value, the request is rejected before processing with 400.
- If the actual cost after processing exceeds it, the request returns 402.

summary.description:
Controls AI-powered content processing. Adds 0.2 credits per successfully extracted URL when enabled.

- `false` - No AI processing, raw extracted content only (default)
- `true` - Generate a text summary of each page
- `"string"` - Generate a summary guided by custom instructions (max 500 characters)
- `{json_schema}` - Extract structured data matching the provided JSON schema

oneOf.description: JSON Schema for structured extraction. Supports types: object, array, string, number, integer, boolean.

extract_effort.description:
Controls how pages are rendered for extraction.

- `"auto"` - Automatically selects the best method per URL (default)
- `"normal"` - HTTP-only extraction, fastest
- `"high"` - Full Chrome rendering, best for JavaScript-heavy pages

start_date.description: Start of the date window for point-in-time extraction. Accepts `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO-8601 datetime. Use with `historical_cache`.

end_date.description: End of the date window (the cutoff) for point-in-time extraction. Accepts `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO-8601 datetime. A year alone means the last day of that year. `start_date` must be on or before `end_date`.

historical_cache.description: Serve a snapshot captured inside the date window instead of a live crawl. On Contents this always applies `historical_cache_strict: "only"`: a URL with no qualifying snapshot fails rather than falling back to a live crawl.

historical_cache_strict.description: Snapshot policy. Accepted for parity with Search, but on Contents any request with `historical_cache: true` uses `only`, whatever value is passed.

screenshot.description: Capture a screenshot of each page. The screenshot URL is returned in each result's `screenshot_url` field.

include_image_links.description: Keep image URLs in the content. When `true` (default), images stay as markdown, for example `![Product photo](https://example.com/p.jpg)`. When `false`, each image becomes `[Image: Product photo]`. The API removes the image URL and keeps the alt text. The API removes an image with no alt text. A linked image `[![alt](src)](href)` becomes `[[Image: alt]](href)`. Other links do not change. Set `false` to use fewer tokens.

max_age.description: The oldest cached copy of a page, in seconds, that you accept. `0` forces a live crawl. Omit it for the default cache policy: a copy up to 7 days old, with a background refresh when it is older than 5 minutes. A value from 1 to 2592000 (30 days) accepts a copy at most that old and starts no background refresh. Cannot be used with `historical_cache`. Works with `async` too. Billing does not change.

async.description: Process URLs asynchronously in the background. Returns a `job_id` to poll via `GET /v1/contents/jobs/{job_id}`. Required when submitting more than 10 URLs (maximum 50). Also useful for slow, JavaScript-heavy pages.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS URL to receive a webhook POST when async processing completes. Only used when `async` is `true`. The webhook payload is signed with HMAC-SHA256.

ContentResult.description: Extracted content from a single URL.

status.description: Processing status for this URL. `not_found` means that the page is a not-found page (a 404 with no real content). Only `success` results are charged.

content.description: Extracted content. Markdown string when `data_type` is `"unstructured"`, JSON object when `data_type` is `"structured"`. Present when `status` is `"success"`.

oneOf.description: Structured data matching the provided JSON schema.

content.example: Placeholder content representing the text returned from a source.

description.example: Illustrative metadata, not a factual research finding.

source.description: `"web"` for web pages, or the dataset id for academic papers served from Valyu's processed index (e.g. `valyu/valyu-arxiv`, `valyu/valyu-pubmed`, `valyu/valyu-biorxiv`, `valyu/valyu-medrxiv`, `valyu/valyu-chemrxiv`).

price.description: Base extraction price for this URL. Excludes the AI add-on for `summary`; use the response's `total_cost_dollars` for the amount charged.

data_type.description: `"unstructured"` for text content, `"structured"` when JSON schema extraction succeeded.

source_type.description: Classification of the content type. `"paper"` for academic papers served from the processed index.

publication_date.description: Publication date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, or empty string if unknown.

cache_state.description: How the page was served. `miss`: this request crawled the page. `hit`: a cached copy answered the request and was fresh for you. `stale`: the page cache served a copy older than 5 minutes for a request with no `max_age`, and the page is refreshed in the background. Papers served from the processed index return `hit`. Present when `status` is `"success"`.

crawled_at.description: Time that the page copy was captured, in ISO 8601. For `miss` it is the crawl time. `null` when there is no page copy to date, for example a paper served from the processed index. Present when `status` is `"success"`.

http_status.description: Present, and always `404`, only when the server answered 404 but the body is the real page. Such a result has `status` `"success"` and is charged like any other success. A not-found template page has `status` `"not_found"` and no `http_status`.

id.description: Identifier for this result. The URL for web pages, or the bare paper id / DOI for academic papers (e.g. `2506.05440`, `10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-chn4j`).

image_url.description: Image URLs found on the page, keyed by index.

screenshot_url.description: Screenshot URL. Present only when `screenshot` was enabled; omitted otherwise.

summary.description: AI-generated summary or structured extraction result. Only present when `summary` was enabled in the request.

summary_success.description: Whether AI processing succeeded. Only present when `summary` was enabled.

structured_metadata.description: Metadata from structured data extraction. Only present when `data_type` is `"structured"`.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason. Only present when `status` is `"failed"` or `"not_found"`. For `not_found` it is `Page not found (404)`. Describes why extraction failed without exposing internal infrastructure.
error.example: Could not extract content from this URL. The page may be unavailable, require sign-in, or block automated access.

doi.description: Paper DOI. Present for academic papers served from the processed index.

authors.description: Paper authors. Present for academic papers served from the processed index.

citation_count.description: Citation count. Present for academic papers served from the processed index.

error.description: Error message if some URLs failed. `null` on complete success.

urls_failed.description: Number of URLs that failed processing.

total_cost_dollars.description: Total amount charged, including any AI add-on. Only successfully extracted URLs are charged.

total_characters.description: Sum of all result content lengths.

ContentsAsyncResponse.description: Response returned when async processing is initiated.

success.description: Whether the async job was created successfully.

urls_total.description: Total number of URLs queued for processing.

poll_url.description: Relative URL to poll for job status.

webhook_secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret for verifying webhook payloads. Only present when `webhook_url` was provided.

job_id.description: Unique identifier for the async job.

status.description:
Current job status.

- `pending` - Job created, not yet started
- `processing` - URLs are being processed
- `completed` - All URLs processed successfully
- `partial` - Processing finished with some failures
- `failed` - All URLs failed. The response still lists every URL in `results`, each with its `status` and `error`.

urls_total.description: Total number of URLs to process.

urls_processed.description: Number of URLs successfully processed so far.

urls_failed.description: Number of URLs that failed processing.

created_at.description: Job creation time as Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time as Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

current_batch.description: Current batch being processed. Only present when `status` is `"processing"`.

total_batches.description: Total number of batches. Only present when `status` is `"processing"`.

results.description: One result for each URL, each with its own `status` and, if the URL did not succeed, an `error`. Present when `status` is `"completed"`, `"partial"` or `"failed"`. A not-found page (a 404 with no real content) is a row with `status` `"not_found"`, not a missing row.

actual_cost_dollars.description: Total cost. Present when the job is finished (`completed`, `partial` or `failed`). It is 0 when no URL succeeded.

error.description: Job-level error message. Can be absent on a `failed` or `partial` job when every failure is per-URL. Read the `error` of each result for the reason.

query.description: The question or research query to answer.
query.example: What are the latest FDA-approved treatments for type 2 diabetes?

search_type.description:
Controls which data sources are searched.

- `all` - Web and proprietary sources (default)
- `web` - Web search only
- `proprietary` - Academic, financial, and premium sources only
- `news` - News articles only

included_sources.description: Sources to include. Accepts domains, URLs, dataset identifiers, or presets (`"finance"`, `"medical"`).

excluded_sources.description: Sources to exclude. Accepts domains, URLs and dataset identifiers. Presets are not supported.

data_max_price.description: Maximum budget for the search component of the answer. It does not cap content extraction or AI processing.

start_date.description: Filter results published on or after this date. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

end_date.description: Filter results published on or before this date. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for geo-targeted search.

fast_mode.description: Enable fast mode for lower latency. Uses 3 tool call rounds instead of 2 and higher result counts per query.

structured_output.description: JSON Schema defining the desired output structure. When set, the AI returns a JSON object matching this schema instead of free-form text. Max depth 10, max 50 properties, max 5000 characters.

system_instructions.description: Custom system instructions for the AI. Replaces the default research agent prompt. Max 2000 characters.
system_instructions.example: You are a medical research assistant. Cite all sources.

search_type.description: Controls which data sources are searched.

source_biases.description: Bias values for specific sources to influence ranking (-5 to +5). Applied to every search call during research.

start_date.description: Filter results from this date. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

end_date.description: Filter results until this date. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be >= `start_date`.

historical_cache.description: With `end_date`, pins the run to that date for backtests: research is limited to sources published by that date, and searches prefer snapshots captured on or before it. Dates before 2026 return a 400.

historical_cache_strict.description: Snapshot policy for a backtest run (`reference_date`, or `end_date` with `historical_cache: true`). Applies to every web search, page read, screenshot and URL in the task. `prefer` uses a snapshot captured at or before the cutoff when one exists, and otherwise reads the live page, so a page can contain text written after the cutoff. `only` never reads a live page: a page with no snapshot at or before the cutoff is dropped. `off` allows live pages without snapshot checks; the cutoff still bounds publication dates. For strict backtests, use `only`. Has no effect when the run has no cutoff.

reference_date.description: Pins the run to this date for backtests, as `historical_cache` does with `end_date`. Takes precedence over `end_date`. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` or an ISO-8601 datetime. Dates before 2026 return a 400.

FileAttachment.description: A file to include in the research task.

data.description: File content as a data URL. Format: `data:<mediaType>;base64,<base64data>`.

context.description: Optional context about the file to guide the research agent. Maximum 50,000 characters per file and 100,000 characters combined across all files.

MCPServerConfig.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration for tool access during research.

url.description: HTTP/HTTPS URL of the MCP server.

name.description: Display name for the MCP server.

tool_prefix.description: Prefix for tool names. Defaults to the server hostname.

allowed_tools.description: Whitelist of tool names to expose. If omitted, all tools are available.

DeepResearchCreateRequest.description:
Request to create a DeepResearch task.

A task can be either **freeform** (provide `query`/`input` plus optional `research_strategy`, `report_format`, etc.) or **workflow-driven** (provide `workflow_id` + `workflow_params`). The two modes are mutually exclusive: passing `workflow_id` alongside freeform fields (`query`, `input`, `research_strategy`, `report_format`) returns `400 workflow_and_freeform_mutually_exclusive`. When running a workflow, any `mode`/`deliverables`/`tools` you pass in the body override the template defaults.

query.description: The research query or question. Use `query` (preferred) or `input` (deprecated). Maximum 25,000 characters. Mutually exclusive with `workflow_id`.
query.example: Comprehensive analysis of CRISPR gene therapy clinical trials in 2024

workflow_id.description: **Beta.** Slug of a workflow to run instead of a freeform query. When set, the task is resolved from the workflow's prompt template using `workflow_params`. Mutually exclusive with freeform fields (`query`, `input`, `research_strategy`, `report_format`); supplying both returns `400 workflow_and_freeform_mutually_exclusive`. See the [Workflows](#tag/Workflows) endpoints.

workflow_params.description: **Beta.** Values for the workflow's template variables, keyed by variable `key`. Required when `workflow_id` is set. Values must satisfy the workflow's declared variable types and validation rules.

workflow_version.description: **Beta.** Pin the run to a specific immutable version of the workflow. Defaults to the workflow's current version when omitted. Only valid with `workflow_id`.

mode.description:
Research mode controlling depth and cost. Prices are credits per task; tool add-ons are extra. See [pricing](https://docs.valyu.ai/pricing).

| Mode | Credits | Best For | Max Steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `instant` | 8 | Short, cited answers in under 30 seconds | 1 |
| `fast` | 25 | Quick queries, batch processing | 12 |
| `standard` | 100 | Balanced research | 25 |
| `heavy` | 500 | Complex topics requiring deep analysis | 45 |
| `max` | 2,500 | Larger research budget for complex tasks | 75 |

strategy.description: **Deprecated.** Use `research_strategy` instead. Natural language strategy to guide the research agent's approach.
strategy.example: Focus on Phase 3 trials and compare efficacy data across studies

research_strategy.description: Natural language strategy to guide the research phase. Controls how the agent searches, what sources to prioritize, and research methodology. Combined length of `research_strategy` and `report_format` must not exceed 15,000 characters.
research_strategy.example: Focus on Phase 3 trials and compare efficacy data across studies

report_format.description: Natural language instructions for the output format. Has highest priority and overrides default formatting. Controls structure, style, length, and presentation of the final report. Combined length of `research_strategy` and `report_format` must not exceed 15,000 characters.
report_format.example: Write a 2-page executive summary with bullet points and a comparison table

urls.description: URLs to include in the research context. Max 10.

files.description: Files to analyze as part of the research. Max 10.

output_formats.description:
Desired output formats. Defaults to `["markdown"]`.

- `"markdown"` - Markdown report (default)
- `"pdf"` - PDF document (can combine with `"markdown"`)
- `"toon"` - Token-efficient structured output; requires a JSON Schema object to also be supplied
- JSON Schema object - Structured JSON output

A JSON Schema object cannot be combined with `"markdown"` or `"pdf"`. `"toon"` requires a JSON Schema object.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata to attach to the task.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers to provide additional tools during research. Max 5.

code_execution.description: Deprecated: use tools.code_execution instead. Enable code execution capability.

tools.description: Controls which optional tools the research agent can use. Each tool accepts an object with `enabled` (boolean, default true) and optional `max_calls` (integer, capped at system default).

max_calls.description: Max invocations per task. Capped at system default (10).

code_execution.description: Enable code execution in a sandboxed Python environment. System default max_calls: 10.

max_calls.description: Max invocations per task. Capped at system default (15).

screenshots.description: Enable visual screenshot capture of web pages. System default max_calls: 15.

max_calls.description: Max invocations per task. Capped at system default (5).

browser_use.description: Enable autonomous browser sessions. System default max_calls: 5.

max_calls.description: Max invocations per task. Charts default is unlimited; this field is accepted for consistency.

charts.description: Enable chart and graph generation embedded in the final report. Free, no per-call surcharge. Unlimited per task.

previous_reports.description: DeepResearch task IDs to use as context for this task. Max 3.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS URL to receive a webhook POST when the task completes. Signed with HMAC-SHA256.

oneOf.description: Email address to notify on completion.

email.description: Email address to notify on completion. Must belong to your organization.

custom_url.description: Custom URL template for the report link in the email. Must contain {id} which gets replaced with the deepresearch task ID.

alert_email.description: Email notification on completion. Pass a string (email address) or an object with email and optional custom_url. The custom_url must contain {id} which gets replaced with the task ID. Email must belong to your organization.

brand_collection_id.description: Brand kit to apply to the PDF report and the deliverables. Send a kit ID from the Valyu platform, or `"none"` for no branding. If you don't send it, the organisation's default kit applies to the report and any deliverables, if the default kit is ready. Brand kits need the Comfortably Pro, Serious Business or Enterprise plan. See [Brand kits](/guides/deepresearch-brand-kits).

deliverables.description: Deliverable files to generate from the research (e.g. Excel reports, presentations). Max 10.

items.description: A deliverable to generate from the research. Can be a string (natural language description, max 500 chars) or a structured object.

oneOf.description: Natural language description of the deliverable.

description.description: Description of what the deliverable should contain.

columns.description: Suggested column names for tabular deliverables (csv, xlsx).

hitl.description: Human-in-the-loop configuration. Enable checkpoints that pause execution at key decision points. Not available for batch requests.

planning_questions.description: Pause before research to ask clarifying questions.

plan_review.description: Pause after planning for user to review the research plan.

source_review.description: Pause after research for user to filter sources by domain.

outline_review.description: Pause after source review for user to review the report outline.

DeepResearchCreateResponse.description: Response after creating a DeepResearch task.

deepresearch_id.description: Unique identifier for the research task.

status.description: Initial task status. `"running"` if started immediately, `"queued"` if waiting for capacity.

mode.description: Research mode used for this task.

public.description: Whether the task is publicly accessible.

webhook_secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret for verifying webhook payloads. Only present when `webhook_url` was provided.

message.description: Status message. Present when task is queued.

warnings.description: Problems with the request itself, for example named datasets outside your plan or a tool the mode doesn't have. The task still runs. New warning types may be added at any time. See [Warnings](https://docs.valyu.ai/api-reference/warnings).

snippet.description: Relevant text excerpt from the source.

description.description: Brief description or snippet from the source.

word_count.description: Word count of the source document.

fragment.description: Optional URL fragment that, when appended to `url`, produces a deep-link to the cited passage on the source page. For HTML sources this is a Scroll-to-Text-Fragment directive (`#:~:text=...`); for PDF sources it uses PDF Open Parameters (`#page=N&search=...`). Build deep-links by concatenating `url + fragment`. Omitted when no reliable highlight target is available - clients should fall back to the canonical `url` in that case.

locations.description: Passages from this source that support the citation. Present only when the source has them; computed results over Valyu data have none. Read it from the raw response: the released SDKs do not expose it yet.

excerpt.description: The exact passage from the source.
excerpt.example: The design draught is 16.4 metres at lowest astronomical tide.

page.description: Page number in the source document, when known.

piece.description: Which part of a long document the passage comes from, when the document was read in parts.

DeepResearchImage.description: An image generated during research (chart, AI-generated, or screenshot).

description.example: Placeholder chart demonstrating a generated image record.

source_url.description: Original web page URL. Only present when `image_type` is `"screenshot"`.

captured_at.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when the screenshot was taken. Only present when `image_type` is `"screenshot"`.

Output formats the workflow produces. Items are the strings `"markdown"`, `"pdf"`, or `"toon"`, and/or a single JSON Schema object for structured output. `code` tells you why:

WorkflowBadRequest.description:
The workflow request was invalid. The `error` field carries a machine-readable code and `message` a human-readable explanation.

Common codes:
- `changelog_required` - a changelog is required when publishing a new version
- `unreferenced_template_vars` - a declared variable is not used in the prompt template, or the template references an unknown variable
- `invalid_output_formats` - `output_formats` contained more than one JSON schema, mixed a schema with `markdown`/`pdf`, or used `toon` without a schema
- `field_too_long` - a text field exceeds its limit (64 KB)
- `too_many_variables` - more than 50 variables
- `too_many_deliverables` - more than 20 deliverables
- `workflow_and_freeform_mutually_exclusive` - workflow and freeform fields were both supplied (on the DeepResearch create endpoint)
